In addition, the Branch ensures that commercial laboratory testing used to determine the basis of payment for milk or for screening of milk for drug residues prior to processing is conducted according to required methods to protect consumers and the marketplace.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Specialist II
jobs.description:
About FACS

At FACS, our mission is to make environments safer and healthier for the people who live and work in them. As one of the nation's leading environmental health consulting firms, we help organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. We are built on purpose, partnership, and performance, delivering measurable impact with every client engagement.
Our Values

We live our mission through three core values:
People First:
Support our team and clients, promote professional growth, and value collaboration.
Integrity of the Science:
Deliver accurate, reliable results through objective, evidence-based practices.
Client Relationships for Life:
Build long-term partnerships and help clients address environmental health challenges.

Why Join Us

At FACS, you’ll contribute meaningful work that helps organizations protect their people, assets, and communities. You’ll join a collaborative, entrepreneurial, and mission-driven team that values scientific integrity, strong client relationships, and professional growth.
Ranked "Best Places to Work" for five consecutive years, we invest in your success through training, mentorship, and support for professional certifications, so you can grow, thrive, and build a career with lasting impact.
Curious to see what we do? Meet our team at FACS Experts.
About the Role

The Environmental Health Specialist II is a hands-on, field-based role supporting industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial (mold and moisture) projects. The Specialist performs on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, air sampling, clearances, and project monitoring, and prepares clear, accurate written field reports.
This role may take the lead on assigned projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned, coordinating closely with the Project Manager, contractors, and clients. Local travel to client and project sites is a regular part of the role.
Fieldwork and Reporting

Perform on-site surveys, inspections, assessments, abatement oversight, and monitoring for industrial hygiene, asbestos, and microbial projects.
Perform asbestos air sampling, clearances, and on-site analysis of air samples while adhering to quality-control requirements.
Prepare written field reports and maintain acceptable report turnaround times.
Identify and secure necessary tools and equipment for assigned projects.
Maintain internal QA/QC compliance.

Project Coordination and Communication

Take the lead on projects when Environmental Health Specialists or field technicians are assigned.
Communicate vital project information to Project Managers to support coordination and progress tracking.
Serve as a liaison between the client, Project Manager, and contractor.
Report project progress and provide technical input to the Project Manager.
Obtain and track project numbers for accurate record-keeping.
Adapt the scope of work in the field as needed to accommodate actual conditions or changes during project progression.

Compliance and Contractor Oversight

Review contractor personnel certifications, medical clearances, and other required documentation to ensure compliance with abatement requirements.
Act as a point of contact and meet with regulatory agents in the event of surprise site inspections.

Team Development and Professional Growth

Assist with training and mentoring junior staff.
Attend required internal and external technical training.
Maintain technical certifications.

Experience

Minimum of two years of experience as a field technician conducting field surveys, inspections, assessments, or asbestos-related monitoring work.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office, including Excel, and ability to quickly learn new software and systems.

Education and Credentials

Bachelor of Science in industrial hygiene, health and safety, biological science, physical science, or a related field—or equivalent relevant experience.
Current California Site Surveillance Technician (CSST) certification required.

Preferred Experience

Experience with asbestos abatement monitoring, air sampling, clearances, or indoor environmental quality work.
Experience serving as a field lead or coordinating with contractors, clients, or junior staff.

Physical & Work Requirements

Physical ability to stoop, kneel, climb, crawl, walk, and stand for extended periods in varied work environments while performing sampling activities
Ability to lift and carry equipment weighing up to 50 lbs.
Prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer for documentation and reporting
Must be able to pass a background check, annual medical examinations, and OSHA-required respirator fit tests
Valid driver's license, reliable transportation, and current auto insurance
Ability to travel locally to assigned client and project sites

Compensation and Rewards

Competitive base salary with performance-based bonus structure tied to individual and team achievements
Comprehensive benefits package, including:
Medical coverage with 100% company-paid premiums for employees and their families, plus 50% of the annual deductible covered by the company
401(k) retirement plan with company matching contributions
Vision and dental plan options
Flexible Spending Accounts (health care and dependent care)
Company-sponsored programs including Employee Assistance Program, life and disability insurance, Rocket Lawyer legal services, and mobile phone plan with Verizon
Voluntary benefits options including supplemental life insurance for employees and dependents, short-term disability, hospital, accident, and pet insurance
Generous PTO (3 weeks accrual), paid holidays, volunteer days, and floating holiday
Tuition Reimbursement Program to promote higher education
Paid training and certifications to support career advancement
Incentive Bonus Plan and Donation Matching Program

Wage Transparency

Pay for this position is based on a number of factors including geographic location, relevant knowledge, skills, and experience.
Why Join FACS

If you are a certified CSST or experienced environmental health field professional who enjoys hands-on fieldwork, asbestos and microbial projects, and supporting clients and project teams, we encourage you to apply. This is an opportunity to take on field leadership, develop technically, and grow within a specialized environmental health consulting practice.
Equal Opportunity Employer

Forensic Analytical Consulting Services is an equal-opportunity employer that complies with EEOC rules and regulations. We are committed to diversity, equity, and inclusion and do not discriminate based on race, age, disability, or other non-merit characteristics. We welcome all candidates to apply, including women, people of color, persons with disabilities, and veterans.
Employment Contingency

Employment is contingent upon successful completion of background check and drug screening.

jobs.title: Environmental Health Promotion Coordinator
jobs.description:
About Children's Ground

Children’s Ground is a First Nations organisation. The Children’s Ground Approach is designed and delivered through the leadership of First Nations people. We are committed to systems change to ensure dignity, justice and equity for all children and families. Our work focuses on national reform as well as evidencing a new way of working.

The Children’s Ground Approach is a whole of community, whole of life approach. We privilege First Nations knowledge systems and practice. Over the course of a generation, led by local expertise, we create and deliver an integrated system that is centred on learning, development and wellbeing that responds to the child and their family through the key transition points from pre-birth to young adulthood.

Our approach recognises the cultural, social, and economic strength of our communities. We build on this over a generation to ensure a future for our children and grandchildren that gives them freedom, opportunity and rights to their culture and identity.

Children’s Ground operates in Central Australia and across the Top End, with support provided by a Melbourne-based Shared Services team.

About The Role

This position will provide services to Central Australia, across five different communities in and around Mparntwe – Alice Springs. The Environmental Health Coordinator will work within a multi-disciplinary team with particular focus on delivering Environmental Health Promotion under the Children’s Ground Family Health and Wellbeing Framework Health in the Hands of the People Utnenge, Tyerrtye, Mwerre Atnyenetyeke Iltye Tyerrtye Urrperle–kenhenge to improve health and wellbeing outcomes for communities. T

The Environmental Health Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing two Orange Sky Laundry trucks, the planned schedule of service delivery across various locations in Mparntwe and staff attached to the trucks in community. Environmental health support is also provided through provision of access to cleaning equipment and other items that will support community members to maintain their homes and support security of tenure. Staff training, advocacy and increasing tenant agency are expected outcomes of the position.

Key Responsibilities

Children’s Ground Family Health Model

Work within the Children’s Ground Family Health and Wellbeing Framework Health in the Hands of the People, to improve health and wellbeing outcomes for the communities we work with.
With the community, develop, assess, and monitor environmental health needs, and manage and implement responses to create improved health and wellbeing outcomes for First Nations people across the region
Ensure that the Environmental Health team is accessible to all First Nations people in the communities where we work.
Support the delivery of health and wellbeing information and services in first language and support local cultural knowledge, life, and lore.
Work with the Learning and Wellbeing Team to support the integration of health and wellbeing into daily learning and development initiatives across CG.

Oversight and delivery of key components of the Family health and Wellbeing Framework including:

Ensure OrangeSky laundry trucks and Environmental Health trailers are deployed Monday to Friday. Support attendees to manage the assets appropriately and facilitate their utilisation across the communities.
Roster and supervise laundry and environmental health trailers with local First Nations people in the community.
Development and implementation of environmental health promotion initiatives as identified and prioritised by community, including but not limited to: Laundry, House cleans and Yard Cleans

Local Community Agency and respect for local cultural knowledge and life

Meet regularly with local First Nations families to discuss local aspirations, to inform directions and responsibilities of Children’s Ground.
Ensure participants have access to information and services that will assist them to maintain their tenancies or address tenancy issues.
Encourage and support First Nations, valuing their ideas, strategies and aspirations
Provide mentoring, management, and guidance to staff to develop professional, trusting, and respectful relationships with people in the region.

Our Commitment and Working Environment

Our work is grounded in deep engagement with First Nations communities and in contributing to long‑term systems change. This environment is rich, relational and meaningful, but can also present challenges that affect timelines that may impact your work - including the need to work respectfully to cultural protocols, respond to community priorities, and navigate complex service systems. Team members must be comfortable working in a flexible, adaptive way that honours community‑led processes while managing competing demands.

Children’s Ground is a Child Safe Organisation, placing children’s safety and wellbeing at the centre of our values, we follow the National Principals for Child Safe Organisations.

At Children’s Ground, culture, language, and First Nations knowledge systems are at the forefront of everything we do. We are committed to creating a walking-together environment that is culturally safe, inclusive, and deeply respectful of diversity. We encourage applications from Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples, individuals from diverse cultural and linguistic backgrounds, members of the LGBTQIA+ community, and people living with a disability. We are a flexible workplace and provide reasonable adjustments throughout our recruitment process—if you require support or alternative formats to apply, please reach out to jennifer.wallace@childrensground.org.au.

To ensure our workforce reflects the families we partner with, the filling of this position is intended to constitute a special measure under section 8(1) of the Racial Discrimination Act 1975. While this role is open to all applicants who share our vision for systemic change, applications from Aboriginal and/or Torres Strait Islander candidates will be strongly prioritised. We highly value lived experience, cultural expertise, and deep connections to community alongside professional skills.

We will be reviewing applications on a rolling basis and may close this ad early if we find the right fit. If you are interested in joining us, we warmly encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Work with Us. Change the World.

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

Job Description

AECOM is seeking an experienced Environmental Scientist III / Senior Environmental Scientist
to join our Environmental Remediation Practice in Richmond, California
.

The successful candidate will provide technical leadership and project coordination for environmental investigation, remediation, groundwater monitoring, compliance, and emergency response projects throughout Northern California and the western United States. This position will support a diverse portfolio of industrial, energy, transportation, municipal, and commercial clients while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams of scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience managing environmental field programs, coordinating subcontractors and laboratories, overseeing health and safety compliance, managing environmental data, and preparing technical and regulatory deliverables.

This position will be based in Richmond, California, with opportunities to support projects throughout Northern California and the western United States.

Responsibilities

Technical and Project Leadership

Lead environmental investigation, monitoring, remediation, and compliance projects from planning through execution.
Coordinate field schedules, staffing, subcontractors, laboratory services, equipment, and site logistics.
Develop and implement work plans, sampling plans, health and safety documentation, and project-specific field procedures.
Support project managers with project planning, budgeting, scheduling, resource forecasting, and client communications.
Identify project risks and develop solutions to achieve project objectives while maintaining quality, schedule, and budget commitments.

Groundwater Monitoring and Remediation

Plan and oversee groundwater, soil, sediment, and waste characterization programs.
Manage groundwater monitoring events and environmental sampling activities.
Coordinate remedial investigations, corrective action programs, groundwater treatment systems, and in-situ remediation efforts.
Evaluate environmental data and support development of remedial strategies and technical recommendations.
Ensure field activities are performed in accordance with project requirements and applicable regulations.

Environmental Compliance

Support environmental compliance programs for industrial, infrastructure, remediation, and construction projects.
Conduct environmental inspections, audits, and compliance assessments.
Monitor project activities for compliance with permits, mitigation measures, Environmental Protection Plans (EPPs), and Storm Water Pollution Prevention Plans (SWPPPs).
Coordinate with regulatory agencies, contractors, and stakeholders to support permitting and environmental compliance objectives.

Health and Safety

Implement and enforce site-specific Health and Safety Plans (HASPs), Job Safety Analyses (JSAs), and company safety procedures.
Lead daily safety meetings, hazard assessments, and pre-task planning activities.
Support atmospheric monitoring, radiological monitoring, confined-space activities, and other specialized health and safety requirements.
Promote a strong safety culture through leadership, mentoring, and continuous improvement.

Technical Reporting and Data Management

Prepare and review technical reports, groundwater monitoring reports, regulatory submittals, and field documentation.
Perform QA/QC reviews of environmental data, field records, and project deliverables.
Manage environmental databases and electronic reporting platforms, including EQuIS and GeoTracker.
Support data validation, interpretation, and presentation of technical findings to clients and regulatory agencies.

Team Development

Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior environmental professionals.
Coordinate multidisciplinary teams including environmental scientists, geologists, engineers, biologists, technicians, and subcontractors.
Support staff development through field training, technical mentoring, and knowledge sharing initiatives.

Qualifications

Minimum Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Environmental Science, Geology, Biology, Environmental Engineering, Natural Resources, or a related field and 4+ years environmental consulting or related professional experience (groundwater monitoring, environmental sampling, remediation field activities, and environmental compliance programs, leading project teams, coordinating complex environmental projects, experience preparing technical reports and regulatory deliverables, etc.) or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.
A valid driver’s license is required, along with the ability to pass a Motor Vehicle Records (MVR) check in accordance with company policy.
Employment is contingent upon successfully completing a pre-employment background check and drug screen.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience supporting California environmental remediation programs, including DTSC, RWQCB, and GeoTracker reporting requirements.
Experience at refinery, chemical, manufacturing, terminal, energy, or other industrial facilities, including CERCLA, RCRA, corrective action, and groundwater remediation programs.
Experience managing subcontractors, coordinating multidisciplinary project teams, and supporting emergency response and disaster recovery.
Experience with complex groundwater monitoring and reporting, environmental site investigations, remediation, compliance, and regulatory reporting.
Proficiency in EQuIS, GeoTracker, environmental database management, QA/QC, data validation, technical report preparation, SWPPP compliance, HASPs, JSAs, atmospheric and radiological monitoring.
Relevant training and certifications: current OSHA 40-Hour HAZWOPER, OSHA 8-Hour HAZWOPER Refresher, OSHA Site Supervisor Training, RCRA Hazardous Waste Management Training, Radiation Safety or Radiological Monitoring Training, Confined Space Entry Training, and First Aid/CPR Certification.

Additional Information

AECOM is unable to provide employment visa sponsorship now or in the future for this position.

Position may involve local and regional travel, field assignments, and periodic overnight travel.

At AECOM, we are committed to maintaining a secure and trustworthy recruitment process and take any fraudulent hiring activity seriously. To support this commitment, all newly hired employees are required to attend an in-person Day 1 onboarding at an AECOM office location as a condition of employment.

Offered rate of compensation will be based on individual education, qualifications, experience, and work location. The range for this position is $76000 to $103000.

About AECOM

AECOM is proud to offer comprehensive benefits to meet the diverse needs of our employees. Depending on your employment status, AECOM benefits may include medical, dental, vision, life, AD&D, disability benefits, paid time off, leaves of absences, voluntary benefits, perks, flexible work options, well-being resources, employee assistance program, business travel insurance, service recognition awards, retirement savings plan, and employee stock purchase plan.

AECOM is the global infrastructure leader, committed to delivering a better world. As a trusted professional services firm powered by deep technical abilities, we solve our clients’ complex challenges in water, environment, energy, transportation and buildings. Our teams partner with public- and private-sector clients to create innovative, sustainable and resilient solutions throughout the project lifecycle – from advisory, planning, design and engineering to program and construction management. AECOM is a Fortune 500 firm that had revenue of $16.1 billion in fiscal year 2025. Learn more at aecom.com.

What makes AECOM a great place to work

You will be part of a global team that champions your growth and career ambitions. Work on groundbreaking projects - both in your local community and on a global scale - that are transforming our industry and shaping the future. With cutting-edge technology and a network of experts, you’ll have the resources to make a real impact. Our award-winning training and development programs are designed to expand your technical expertise and leadership skills, helping you build the career you’ve always envisioned. Here, you’ll find a welcoming workplace built on respect, collaboration and community—where you have the freedom to grow in a world of opportunity.

As an Equal Opportunity Employer, we believe in your potential and are here to help you achieve it. All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.

jobs.description:
JOB POSTING

How To Apply

For full consideration, applicants should attach their resume and cover letter when applying for a job opening. For guidance related to the application process or if you are experiencing difficulties when applying, please review the Applicant Resources on our website.

How to Apply
Troubleshooting
Tips for Applicants
FAQ’s

INITIAL REVIEW DATE (IRD)

UC Santa Cruz jobs are posted until filled. All application materials submitted by 11:59 pm on the IRD will be routed to the hiring team for consideration. NOTE: Applicants who miss the IRD are still encouraged to apply; their materials will still be forwarded for consideration if requested by the hiring team. Application materials cannot be accepted outside of the jobs portal. Applications cannot be edited on an applicant's behalf. For more information about the IRD and the applicant review process, view this link.

The IRD for this job is: 11-04-2026

About Uc Santa Cruz

UC Santa Cruz is a public university like no other in California, combining the experience of a small, liberal arts college with the depth and rigor of a major research university. It's known as an unconventional place where innovation and experimentation is part of the campus's DNA. That playful, bold spirit still thrives today, all on a campus renowned as among the most beautiful in the world.

Department Overview

Administratively located within the Finance, Operations, and Administration (FOA) division, our primary duties are to promote, facilitate, and provide expert consultation for EH&S programs in support of university operations. We are responsible for monitoring compliance with environmental, health and safety programs intended to minimize or prevent occupational injuries and illnesses in the workplace and to protect the quality of the surrounding environment. EH&S advises the campus community on responsibilities with respect to health, safety and environmental issues; recommends appropriate corrective actions; and helps implement new health and safety programs. EH&S also acts as liaison between UCSC and various external agencies and regulatory bodies. Our actions and decisions have the potential for high visibility and serious consequences to the campus and the community. EH&S programs include a broad and complex range of disciplines including areas such as laboratory and research safety, industrial hygiene, food safety, environmental management, diving and boating safety, radiation safety, hazardous materials control, ergonomics, biosafety, and fire safety.

More information can be found at: https://ehs.ucsc.edu/

Job Summary

The Hazardous Materials and Waste Manager serves as the technical expert for Hazardous Materials, Hazardous Waste, and Dangerous Goods Shipping. The position is responsible for three Waste Accumulation Areas (WAAs); coordinates chemical, medical, and universal waste collections; manages waste billing and manifest fees; and directly executes dangerous goods shipments. This position is highly active in auditing and reporting, it requires conducting weekly WAA inspections, annual non-lab hazmat inspections, and annual SPCC inspections; processing technical information to produce regulatory reports, such as California Environmental Reporting System (CERS) business plans, annual e-waste reports, and biennial waste reports; and delivers outreach and training to campus waste generators. The position oversees problems that are complex and may require creation of new methodologies by applying professional EH&S knowledge and expertise. They will also serve as the technical expert in the development and implementation of programs within these fields. Decision-making is based on established procedures, integration and interpretation of relevant laws, regulations and organizational policy; professional best practices; relevant science methodology, impact on other EH&S programs; and senior management approvals. Decisions may impact other EH&S programs, departments, segments of the organization and / or organization-wide.

APPOINTMENT INFORMATION

Budgeted Salary:
$100,100 - $107,674/annually. Salary commensurate with skills, qualifications and experience.

Under California law, the University of California, Santa Cruz is required to post a reasonable estimate of the compensation for this role. The salary shown above is the budgeted amount the University reasonably expects to pay and the salary extended should not exceed this posted amount.

Benefits Level Eligibility:
Full benefits

Schedule Information

Full-time, Fixed
Percentage of Time: 100%, 40 Hours per Week
Days of the Week: Mon-Fri
Shift Includes: Day

Employee Classification:
Career appointment

Job End Date:
None

Work Location:
UC Santa Cruz Main Campus

Union Representation:
Non-Represented

Job Code Classification:
EHS SPEC 4 (000358)

Travel:
Never or Rarely

Job Duties

40% - Hazardous Waste Program Management

Performs complex technical work in hazardous materials control, hazardous waste management, and shipping.

Chemical Waste Collection and Management: Weekly consolidation pick-ups, supporting offsite shipments, combined waste management, and chemo waste.
Medical Waste Management: Manage weekly waste pick-ups.
Universal Waste Management: Organize battery pick-ups and shipping.
Dangerous Goods Shipping: Execute dangerous goods shipments; complete shipper's declaration; review package compliance.
Waste Manifests Management: Organize and maintain official waste manifests.
Taxes and Fees: Ensure all waste manifest taxes and fees are allocated and paid appropriately.

Drafts reports and other documentation.

Waste Biennial Reporting: Gather data and write biennial waste reports.
Hazardous Materials Business Plan: Draft annual report, including its detailed inventories and maps.
E-waste Annual Report: Coordinate data collection and drafting the annual report on electronic waste.
Hazardous Materials Business Plan: Manage CERS (California Environmental Reporting System) compliance and program requirements.

20% - Outreach and Education

Performs outreach and communication to UCSC affiliate populations.

Waste and Hazmat Training: Design and provide training on related topics - Waste Generator and Manifests, WAA training, and Hazardous Materials Management.
Billing and Invoice Management: Handle billing, invoices, and consolidated billing for chemical waste, medical waste, and batteries.

Writes and updates manuals and procedures.

Maintain accurate and approachable online resources for hazardous materials and hazardous waste safety.

Provides expert counsel by evaluating, interpreting and applying laws, regulations, codes and standards.

Waste Evaluations: Provide evaluations of waste types and properties to determine proper handling and disposal protocols.

20% - Inspections and Compliance

Monitors compliance and prevents hazards, and may serve as organization liaison with regulatory agencies.

CUPA Inspection Liaison: Coordinate and manage agency inspection and corrective action follow-ups.
WAA (Waste Accumulation Area) Management: Oversee WAA operations, ensuring a clean, functional, and well-maintained facilities.

Inspects, investigates incidents and complaints, and recommends corrective action as needed.

Non-Lab Hazmat Inspections: Carry out inspections on non-research facilities that store hazardous chemicals, validate chemical inventories, monitor and support corrective actions.
SPCC Plan Annual Inspections: Perform annual inspections required for Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure plans.

15% - Program Improvement

May represent EH&S regarding hazardous materials and waste, and dangerous goods shipping at meetings and conferences involving academic compliance committees, campus, system wide, local government, state and federal levels of authority.

Participate in the systemwide Hazardous Waste Action Group (HWAG).
Review of Systemwide and CHWMEG Reports: Independent audits and environmental risk assessments of third-party waste disposal and recycling vendors.
Maintain DOT and IATA shipper training.

Develops procedures using a combination of original and standard professional approaches / techniques to solve substantive, complex problems with multiple variables.

Vendor Management: Manage waste vendor relations and ensure accurate waste profiles.

Applies appropriate scientific and professional standards to recommend organization / university policies and programs and, as needed, create new methodologies.

Waste Minimization Compliance: Evaluate and structure processes to ensure compliance with Waste Minimization (SB 14) regulations.

5% - Incident Response and Support

Participate as a member of the EH&S incident response team. Provides support to campus disaster preparedness activities, responds to hazardous materials releases and serves in the appropriate response role based on training and expertise.

Inventory management of response equipment, ordering consumable spill response materials, and keeping the emergency response truck stocked.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training

jobs.description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

**The Opportunity:**

We are seeking an experienced senior toxicologist, who combines scientific excellence with strategic leadership, for our Toxicology group within the Nonclinical Development and Clinical Pharmacology (NDCP) Department, to work in close collaboration with Research and Development colleagues on new and ongoing portfolio projects. Working within a highly collaborative, cross-functional organization, this role provides toxicology leadership from early research through all stages of clinical development, ensuring that safety assessments enable informed development decisions and global regulatory filings. The successful candidate will:

* Lead nonclinical safety strategy for multiple drug development programs spanning both small molecules and biologics.
* Serve as the toxicology representative on cross-functional Research and Development project teams, providing scientific guidance and influencing development strategy.
* Design, oversee, interpret, and communicate toxicology studies that support candidate selection, IND-enabling activities, and regulatory submissions.
* Author and review regulatory documents and ensure compliance with GLP, ICH, and global regulatory requirements.
* Provide expert interpretation of toxicology data within the context of the current scientific approaches/best practices, project objectives, and benefit-risk assessment.
* Lead nonclinical development sub-teams, mentor colleagues, and contribute to departmental strategy and process improvements.
* Collaborate with investigative toxicology team to drive mechanistic studies for target-, pathway- or off-target toxicities using in vitro and in vivo studies, including emerging new approach methodologies (NAMS) such as cell- and organoid-based assays and advanced imaging analyses.
* Drive innovation, solve complex scientific problems, and effectively manage multiple programs in a fast-paced environment.

**Required Skills, Experience and Education:**

* PhD in Toxicology or a related discipline with 10+ years, or M.S. degree with 15+ years, of relevant experience in the biopharmaceutical industry; DABT certification is desirable.
* Deep expertise in nonclinical safety assessment for small molecules and other modalities.
* Strong understanding of toxicology study design, GLPs, global regulatory requirements, with experience interacting with global regulatory authorities.
* Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams, influence strategy, and communicate effectively across scientific disciplines to resolve complex safety questions and support project decision-making.
* Strong scientific background and scientific aptitude with excellent critical thinking skills.

**Preferred Skills:**

* Expertise in integrating mechanistic, translational, and biomarker-based safety assessments into nonclinical development programs.
* Familiarity with impurity risk assessment, product quality, occupational and/or environmental toxicology, or in silico/computational toxicology.

jobs.title: Environmental Science Educator - Yosemite
jobs.description:
**Have you always wanted to work in a National Park? Are you a passionate, dedicated educator who is enthusiastic about working with youth? NatureBridge offers full-time educator positions with health benefits, housing, and paid time off. Apply today!**

**About the Position**

NatureBridge provides overnight environmental science education experiences for more than 30,000 students and their teachers every year in the world’s best classrooms: our National Parks. Our mission is to connect young people to the science and wonder of the natural world, igniting self-discovery, and inspiring stewardship of the planet. Through our programs, students explore the outdoors, connect with their peers, discover themselves and develop a lasting relationship with science and the environment around them.

**NatureBridge Educator Schedule -** **Video: What is it like to work at NatureBridge?**

Environmental Science Educator (ESE) schedule varies week-to-week. ESEs can expect to deliver environmental science and team-building programs from 9am - 4pm for 3-5 day programs Monday - Friday, with variability during schools’ arrival and departure days. ESEs also run evening programs 2-3 times a week from 6:30pm - 8:30pm. On a regular program day, the ESE receives up to 30 minutes of paid preparation time. ESEs attend regular meetings with other ESEs, and the education and operations teams to discuss program updates and collaborative feedback to the community workplace. In addition to educational responsibilities, ESEs help in other departments when needed or asked.

**Tasks and functions**

During Program:

* Lead multi-day, student-centered, experiential environmental science programs in outdoor settings.
* Facilitate inclusive, culturally relevant instruction that incorporates multiple perspectives and connects learning to students’ lives and communities.
* Engage students in scientific practices through hands-on investigations, while tailoring programming to meet the specific needs of each school group, align with teacher-defined outcomes, and reflect the NatureBridge Theory of Change.
* Follow NatureBridge risk management policies and procedures, and use sound judgment to make decisions and manage risk while managing students’ physical and emotional well-being when leading groups in outdoor settings. Administer and document first aid as necessary and appropriate, and document as required by NatureBridge.
* Foster a supportive, respectful learning environment and model responsible environmental behavior.
* Design and lead evening programs or assist guest presenters and partners, typically twice weekly following the field day.

Outside of Program:

* Serve as an educator on standby when scheduled.
* Assess and document student learning; contribute to program reflection, evaluation and improvement.
* Participate in staff meetings, training sessions, and program debriefs and complete all required paperwork in a timely fashion.
* Maintain gear and contribute to campus stewardship.
* Contribute to fundraising efforts by sharing stories from the field.
* For staff in NatureBridge Housing: Follow all housing policies and co-created community agreements.
* Build respectful, supportive relationships with staff, volunteers, and participants and provide high-quality customer service.
* Support campus operations and organizational goals through additional duties as assigned, such as event support, special projects, and community stewardship.

**Compensation:**

* $17.14/hour, daily and weekly work hours vary based on programming demand.
* On-site housing may be provided as a benefit of employment.
* Medical, dental and vision insurance
* Option for a 403b retirement plan with employer match after six months
* Paid vacation, training days, and sick leave
* Other benefits include Employee Assistance Plan (EAP), Flexible Spending Account (FSA) and more
* See an example of our Golden Gate housing Here. Housing varies by campus.

**Eligibility Requirements and Qualifications**

We are looking for candidates who have:

* At least 1 year of relevant formal or informal teaching experience
* The social and emotional skills to build rapport and positive relationships with people from all backgrounds, abilities, cultures, orientations, identities and communities.
* A demonstrated commitment to equity and inclusion within your teaching and workplace community. We especially encourage you to apply if you have lived experience as a member of (and/or extensive experience working with people from) any communities that are impacted by the historic and current system of oppression that has limited access to environmental education or the outdoors in general.
* The ability to communicate clearly to different groups, including students, coworkers, supervisors and educational partners.
* A desire to learn and grow, and an openness to feedback and coaching.
* Capacity to pivot quickly and manage logistical changes with composure
* A valid **Wilderness First Responder Certification** or a willingness to attain the certification prior to the start date. Tuition aid is available to hired candidates to offset costs of a re/certification.
* The ability and willingness to perform physically challenging work outdoors and in all weather conditions on uneven terrain; able to hike 5-7 miles in uneven terrain
* Ability to work flexible hours and split shifts, including evenings.

**If you are interested in the role and do not meet every requirement listed, please still apply! We are interested in applicants with unique lived experience and skill sets.**

* Employment eligibility is contingent on successful completion of a background check.

**Why should you join the NatureBridge team?**

* We are a mission-driven organization that values your contributions and supports you in making a positive impact on youth and the environment
* You will get to work in a beautiful natural setting with other dedicated educators who are passionate about the environmen

jobs.description:
Research Data Analyst 1 (5272C), Environmental Science, Policy, and Management #89414 About Berkeley
  
  
At the University of California, Berkeley , we are dedicated to fostering a community where everyone feels welcome and can thrive. Our culture of openness, freedom, and belonging makes it a special place for students, faculty, and staff, who are among the most talented and accomplished anywhere, including Nobel laureates, Pulitzer Prize winners, and MacArthur Fellows. Since our founding in 1868, we have been an engine for innovation - driving intellectual, economic, and social progress that benefits California, the U.S., and beyond. Together, we change the world.
  
  
At Berkeley, the best careers are built on a foundation of continuous learning and growth . We actively support professional development by providing all full-time staff employees with at least 80 hours of paid time per year and provide space for supportive colleague communities via numerous employee resource groups.
  
  
We invite applicants who are inspired by our Principles of Community and who are eager to be part of our exciting Strategic Plan , which charts Berkeley's next era of excellence.
  
  
Learn more about some of our accomplishments at Points of Pride .
  
  
Departmental Overview
  
  
The Department of Environmental Science, Policy, and Management is home to multidisciplinary research programs that recognize the urgency of the challenges-and the enormous opportunities-that may lead to transformative change. We have award-winning faculty in climate science, biodiversity, environmental policy, land use, and community outreach who are all driven by a collective interest in our environmental future.
  
  
Position Summary
  
  
The Coastal Climate Resilience Lab (PI Rachel Carlson) seeks a Research Data Analyst 1 in the area of remote sensing and geospatial analysis. This is a part-time position (20 hours per week).
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 will conduct data analysis supporting two ongoing research collaborations:
  
  
Remote sensing of freshwater plumes in California (PI Carlson and co-PIs Albert Ruhi and Kelly Hondula)
  
Effects of land use and land cover on nearshore marine environments (PI Carlson).
  
  
This position involves preparing and analyzing ecological datasets using established remote sensing and geospatial methods under the direct supervision of other researchers. The Research Data Analyst 1 will apply data science and quantitative modeling methods to map freshwater flux in the marine environment and evaluate interlocking patterns in human-dominated landscapes and benthic ecosystems. This position works in a team to coordinate data cleaning, quality control, and code documentation, complete computational analysis, and prepare data visualizations displaying analytical results for internal review.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would be based in the research laboratory of PI Dr. Rachel Carlson on the UC Berkeley campus. They would also be co-mentored by Dr. Albert Ruhi (co-PI, ESPM, Berkeley) and remotely by Dr. Kelly Hondula (Arizona State University). They would receive additional guidance from at least one PhD student. Remote working arrangements are considered.
  
  
The Research Data Analyst 1 would have the opportunity to participate in campus data science, wilderness first aid, and other professional development opportunities. They would have the opportunity to attend one USA-based conference each year. The PI's group provides a supportive work environment that recognizes and supports people of diverse identities and needs and prioritizes inclusive practices and field safety.
  
  
Application Review Date
  
  
The First Review Date for this job is October 26, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
  
  
Responsibilities
  
  
50%
  
  
Under direct supervision, performs basic statistical and data analysis.
  
Apply existing code to new data found from an online repository to deliver code outputs.
  
Apply an existing code script (existing method) to data on inputs to the California coastline.
  
Create reports and basic visualizations on results.
  
  
15%
  
  
Supports testing of research instruments and data sources.
  
Using standard geospatial software/tools and under direct supervision, create a map of tree species using an established method and protocol.
  
  
10%
  
  
Collects research data and prepares it for analysis.
  
  
10%
  
  
Assists with study design proposals and survey instruments.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with report preparation and / or analysis for internal constituents.
  
  
5%
  
  
Develops knowledge in areas of storage, documentation and dissemination of computerized data.
  
  
5%
  
  
Assists with evaluation and research of data reporting products.
  
  
Required Qualifications
  
  
Acquiring knowledge of research function. Acquiring ability to perform research analysis duties.
  
Acquiring statistical analysis, systems programming, and database design skills to perform research analysis duties.
  
Ability to effectively manage time and see assigned parts of projects through to completion on deadline.
  
Basic consultation and communication skills.
  
  
Education / Training
  
  
Bachelor's degree in related area and / or equivalent experience / training. (Required)
  
  
Salary & Benefits
  
  
For information on the comprehensive benefits package offered by the University, please visit the University of California's Compensation & Benefits website.

APTIM Environmental & Infrastructure, LLC is seeking an Environmental Scientist on a full-time basis out of Bakersfield, CA to participate in a variety of environmental compliance tasks in support of our RCRA and state hazardous waste, non-RCRA waste, regulated waste, hazardous materials management, stormwater and other environmental compliance media including auditing programs. The successful candidate will prepare technical and compliance reports, conduct technical and regulatory analyses and perform diverse fieldwork, including sampling inspections and audits. Be expected to maintain current knowledge of environmental regulations and emerging developments. This role requires both independent work and collaboration with multidisciplinary teams to ensure compliance and provide clients with practical, science-based solutions. This position will primarily be 50% office and 50% field requiring travel to client facilities conduct environmental compliance reviews/audits and/or gather related data.

* Executing and managing various work scopes, while meeting project schedules and budgets.
* Collection and interpretation/evaluation of scientific data.

* Draft technical documents for regulatory agencies and private clients.
* Communications with regulatory agencies.
* Time management to ensure a quality product is prepared to meet project deadlines.
* Applying knowledge and skills to a wide range of standard and nonstandard situations.
* Following defined processes explicitly while also being able to identify and accommodate new or changing scenarios as well as developing processes for new activities.

By Mail

### **Job Description and Duties**

Delta Smelt and Longfin smelt are unique fishes of the San Francisco Estuary and have recently declined to their lowest population levels since monitoring began over 60 years ago. These species sit at the center of California's water management challenges, where the goal is to balance human water needs with the ecological needs of native fish. To better manage and protect these species, a highly skilled team of multi-disciplinary scientists collaborates across agencies to improve our understanding of Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt life history, identify key stressors, and develop creative strategies to minimize and mitigate impacts associated with freshwater exports.

This position offers a unique opportunity for an individual with strong leadership skills and a background in fisheries biology and the California Endangered Species Act to lead the Smelt Team within the California Department of Fish and Wildlife's State Water Project Permitting Program. The Smelt Team Supervisor will oversee implementation of, and compliance with, the federal and state endangered species acts for the Central Valley Project (CVP), State Water Project (SWP), and the Delta Conveyance Project (DCP). They will collaborate with State, federal, academic, and/or colleagues to implement and review the scientific and administrative aspects of water project operations, covered species monitoring, scientific study, and mitigation. The Smelt Team Supervisor will also lead the team in developing novel monitoring, minimization, and mitigation concepts for Delta Smelt and Longfin Smelt and propose them to Water Branch management for implementation.

  
The mission of the State Water Project Permitting Unit is to develop and implement novel, science-based solutions to conflicts between water supply and ecosystem management in the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta and tributaries. We will consistently provide clear, creative, and feasible solutions to conserve and adaptively manage imperiled species and ecosystems impacted by joint operations of the State and federal water projects. We will do this by developing our own scientific expertise and encouraging outside-the-box thinking in a collaborative, open, respectful, and candid setting.

**Work with Us. Change the World.**

At AECOM, we're delivering a better world. Whether improving your commute, keeping the lights on, providing access to clean water, or transforming skylines, our work helps people and communities thrive. We are the world's trusted infrastructure consulting firm, partnering with clients to solve the world’s most complex challenges and build legacies for future generations.

There has never been a better time to be at AECOM. With accelerating infrastructure investment worldwide, our services are in great demand. We invite you to bring your bold ideas and big dreams and become part of a global team of over 50,000 planners, designers, engineers, scientists, digital innovators, program and construction managers and other professionals delivering projects that create a positive and tangible impact around the world.

We're one global team driven by our common purpose to deliver a better world. Join us.

 **Job Description**

AECOM is seeking an experienced **Environmental Scientist III / Senior Environmental Scientist** to join our Environmental Remediation Practice in **Richmond, California**.

The successful candidate will provide technical leadership and project coordination for environmental investigation, remediation, groundwater monitoring, compliance, and emergency response projects throughout Northern California and the western United States. This position will support a diverse portfolio of industrial, energy, transportation, municipal, and commercial clients while collaborating with multidisciplinary teams of scientists, engineers, geologists, and technical specialists.

The ideal candidate will have strong experience managing environmental field programs, coordinating subcontractors and laboratories, overseeing health and safety compliance, managing environmental data, and preparing technical and regulatory deliverables.

**This position will be based in Richmond, California, with opportunities to support projects throughout Northern California and the western United States.**

**Responsibilities**

**Technical and Project Leadership**

* Lead environmental investigation, monitoring, remediation, and compliance projects from planning through execution.
* Coordinate field schedules, staffing, subcontractors, laboratory services, equipment, and site logistics.
* Develop and implement work plans, sampling plans, health and safety documentation, and project-specific field procedures.
* Support project managers with project planning, budgeting, scheduling, resource forecasting, and client communications.
* Identify project risks and develop solutions to achieve project objectives while maintaining quality, schedule, and budget commitments.

**Groundwater Monitoring and Remediation**

* Plan and oversee groundwater, soil, sediment, and waste characterization programs.
* Manage groundwater monitoring events and environmental sampling activities.
* Coordinate remedial investigations, corrective action programs, groundwater treatment systems, and in-situ remediation efforts.
* Evaluate environmental data and support development of remedial strategies and technical recommendations.
* Ensure field activities are performed in accordance with project requirements and applicable regulations.

**Environmental Compliance**

* Support environmental compliance programs for industrial, infrastructure, remediation, and construction projects.

* Promote a strong safety culture through leadership, mentoring, and continuous improvement.

* Prepare and review technical reports, groundwater monitoring reports, regulatory submittals, and field documentation.
* Perform QA/QC reviews of environmental data, field records, and project deliverables.
* Manage environmental databases and electronic reporting platforms, including EQuIS and GeoTracker.
* Support data validation, interpretation, and presentation of technical findings to clients and regulatory agencies.

* Mentor and provide technical guidance to junior environmental professionals.
* Coordinate multidisciplinary teams including environmental scientists, geologists, engineers, biologists, technicians, and subcontractors.
* Support staff development through field training, technical mentoring, and knowledge sharing initiatives.

Central Highlands Water is a major regional employer, and we want you to join us!

About Us

At CHW we provide drinking water, sewerage, trade waste and recycled water services to residents and businesses in the Central Highlands region of Victoria. We are a public sector employer with a proud history spanning more than 150 years of supporting regional prosperity through service excellence.

Central Highlands Water is a growing business which strives to create a thriving and sustainable region by providing the highest quality water related service to our diverse customer base. This opportunity is a vital role to shape the future of how our services support our community.

To learn more about CHW and how our everyday people contribute to the Central Highlands region of Victoria, visit our website
, or check out our LinkedIn
or Instagram
pages!

The opportunity

Requirements

The primary objective of the Senior Technical Officer – Distribution Water Quality role is to develop and monitor the delivery of strategies and programs to ensure CHW and regulatory water quality requirements are delivered upon across the drinking water distribution network. Key duties include:

Disinfectant residual management within the network distribution system, including storage and distribution tanks and management of water age.
Monitor the delivery of distribution system pipe and tanks/basins inspection and cleaning programs, assess the effectiveness of the programs and ensure water quality related outcomes are actioned.
Take a lead role in responding to distribution system water quality incidents e.g. microbial, taste and odour, security breaches, discolouration, backflow events and other possible contamination incidents.
Coordinate the development and delivery of training/education programs and mentor maintenance delivery teams in the application of water quality controls to distribution maintenance activities.
Develop and implement a risk-based distribution system wide real time water quality monitoring strategy.
Work collaboratively with the proactive and reactive maintenance functions to incorporate water quality outcomes within maintenance programs.

About You

Safety is our No. 1 priority, and we expect you will actively contribute to and foster a 'safety first' culture that supports our aspiration of zero harm. This means you care deeply about the physical and psychological safety of people so that our team return home in great shape at the end of the day.

We’d love to hear from you if you have:

Relevant qualifications, experience, specialist knowledge and skills.
Knowledge and demonstrated experience in water quality management within a water supply system.
Demonstrated highly developed organisational and communication skills with exceptional attention to detail.
Proven experience in leading teams and the ability to deliver on water quality outcomes
Proven knowledge of safety, water quality and environmental regulations.

What's in it for you?

Working for one of the region's largest employers you will be part of an organisation that is high achieving, cohesive and always striving for better customer outcomes. We're full of "everyday people" that are great to work with and reflect our community!

We're offering a supportive environment and offer a huge range of employee options and benefits. There's the option of work hybrid, including a mix of being in our office in Ballarat, as well as the flexibility to work from home. Other benefits include accrued time off, generous leave options, professional development, industry collaboration, health and wellbeing programs and a supportive management team.

At CHW You Will

Have access to training and development opportunities that will further develop your knowledge and skills.
Be part of an organisation that strongly promotes work life balance, flexibility, safety and wellbeing.
Work in an organisation that makes a difference to our community.
Be part of an organisation that cares about you, your safety and wellbeing.

If you want to make a positive impact through meaningful work and have the energy, courage and ideas to take on a challenge, we’d love to hear from you! To submit your application, click on APPLY to be redirected to our website and for a copy of the Position Description. While you are on our website, take a look around. You won't be disappointed!

Please ensure you provide a cover letter and your resume.

Have questions?

For a confidential chat about the role, please contact Bridget Clark on 0428 725 983.

Applications close 5:00pm Friday 23 October 2026.

Please note, as part of our selection process, we conduct pre-appointment checks including those related to references, identity, fitness to work, qualifications, work history, work visa, misconduct and police record history.
This role may be subject to a probation period.

We welcome applications from people with disability and aim to provide an inclusive and accessible workplace. If you need any help with the application process or would like to discuss your reasonable adjustments during interviews, please contact Brenda Wong.

If you need a copy of this advertisement in an accessible format, please email applications@chw.net.au

**Job Summary**

The HRA Coordinator is a non-licensed, non-clinical team member responsible for conducting Health Risk Assessments (HRAs) and supporting member outreach activities for Dual Eligible Special Needs Plan (D-SNP) members. This position serves as the primary resource for HRA outreach, assessment completion, risk stratification, and identification of health-related and social needs. Through telephonic outreach and standardized assessments, the HRA Coordinator identifies low-, medium-, and high-risk members and facilitates referrals to Care Coordination, Care Management, and other appropriate programs for further intervention and support. This position may provide backup support for D-SNP Care Coordinator functions as operational needs require.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

**Health Risk Assessment Administration and Member Outreach, with duties including but not limited to:**

* Conduct telephonic Health Risk Assessments with D-SNP members and authorized representatives.
* Complete initial and annual HRAs within established regulatory and organizational timeframes.
* Perform inbound and outbound member outreach to schedule and complete assessments.
* Explain the purpose and benefits of the HRA process and encourage member participation.
* Gather and document information related to health status, chronic conditions, medications, healthcare utilization, behavioral health, functional limitations, caregiver support, and social needs.
* Verify member eligibility, demographic and contact information.
* Utilize approved assessment tools, workflows, scripts, and department protocols.
* Establish rapport and maintain professional interactions with members, caregivers, providers, and internal stakeholders.
* Utilize interpreter services as needed to effectively communicate with members.
* Maintain assigned outreach inventories and assessment workloads to meet productivity standards.

**2. Risk Stratification and Needs Identification, with duties including but not limited to:**

* Review HRA findings to identify health risks, barriers to care, and unmet member needs.
* Stratify members into low-, medium-, and high-risk categories utilizing established departmental criteria.
* Evaluate assessment findings to identify member risk levels, health-related needs, functional limitations, behavioral health concerns, and social determinants of health (SDOH) barriers.
* Identify opportunities for intervention through Care Coordination, Care Management, Social Work, Community Health Workers, Pharmacy, Behavioral Health, LTSS, and other supportive programs.
* Assess for social determinants of health concerns including food insecurity, transportation barriers, housing instability, caregiver support needs, and access to healthcare services.
* Recognize indicators of frequent emergency department utilization, recent hospitalizations, chronic disease burden, medication concerns, functional impairments, behavioral health needs, and fall risk.
* Identify members requiring additional assessment or clinical review.
* Prioritize referrals based on risk level and member needs.
* Communicate significant findings to appropriate care team members.

**3. Referral Management and Care Coordination Support, with duties including but not limited to:**

* Generate referrals to Care Coordination, Care Management, Social Work, Community Health Workers, Behavioral Health, and other internal programs based on assessment findings.
* Facilitate referrals to community-based organizations and supportive services.
* Transfer identified members to the appropriate care team for ongoing engagement and intervention.
* Collaborate with Care Coordinators, RN Care Managers, Social Workers, and other interdisciplinary team members to ensure smooth member transitions.
* Escalate urgent clinical, safety, behavioral health, abuse, neglect, or other high-risk concerns according to established policies and procedures.
* Monitor assigned referral activities and support closure of referral loops when appropriate.
* Assist with member outreach, scheduling, appointment coordination, and other non-clinical care coordination activities as assigned.
* Provide backup support for D-SNP Care Coordinator responsibilities during staffing shortages, peak workloads, or operational needs.

* Maintain confidentiality and protect member information in compliance with HIPAA and organizational policies.
* Monitor assigned work queues and complete tasks within established turnaround times.
* Assist with audit preparation, reporting activities, and quality review processes.
* Monitor HRA completion rates and support initiatives designed to improve member outreach and engagement.
* Participate in team meetings, trainings, and quality improvement activities.

jobs.description:
Position Information

Sonoma Water is seeing a passionate and driven Environmental Specialist I professional to join our team!

Join us in protecting and enhancing Sonoma County’s natural resources through meaningful, impactful work.

The Sonoma Water Agency is seeking a qualified candidate to fill a Water Agency Environmental Specialist I position responsible for working on environmental compliance and permitting matters for Sonoma Water projects.

Responsibilities

At Sonoma Water, Environmental Specialists are responsible for evaluating, analyzing, and reporting on the environmental impacts of water supply, flood control, sanitation, and sustainability projects. To comply with federal, state, and local regulations, these positions assist in developing and proposing mitigation strategies to avoid, reduce, or offset the environmental impacts of projects. The Environmental Specialist I also uses an interdisciplinary approach from applied knowledge of biology, ecology, environmental science, and hydrology to:

Assist with the preparation of California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) studies, such as categorical exemptions, mitigated negative declarations, environmental impact reports, and technical resource reports
Assist with preparation of environmental regulatory permit applications to local, state, and federal resource agencies
Perform field assessments and surveys for sensitive resources, such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife, botanical, and fisheries resources to evaluate environmental effects and determine potential impacts from projects
Review natural resource studies and reports to understand historical and current site conditions of a project
Review project information, schedules, studies, and designs, and assist in preparing tracking tools, standard operating procedures, and reports for projects
Assist in the preparation and review of documents to comply with state, federal, and local environmental laws and regulations; land use planning projects; grant applications; and right-of-way activities
Stay up to date with environmental laws such as the CEQA, National Environmental Protection Act (NEPA), Clean Water Act, Porter-Cologne Water Quality Control Act, California and Federal Endangered Species Acts

About

The ideal candidate for this position is a team player and passionate about the environment and its resources. They will possess strong communication, problem-solving, and project organizational skills. In addition, they will possess experience conducting many of the following activities:

Knowledge of and experience with handling threatened, endangered, and/or sensitive species listed under state or federal endangered species acts (such as California red-legged frog, California tiger salamander, steelhead trout, and California freshwater shrimp)
Conducting field assessments and investigations for natural resources such as aquatic and terrestrial habitat features, wildlife and botanical resources in remote areas (e.g. agricultural lands, meadowlands, forests, and aquatic and riparian habitats)
Collecting, analyzing, and reporting on environmental scientific data associated with natural resources, specifically wildlife
Researching the historical land uses, existing conditions, and natural resources of a project site, and associated local, state, and federal regulations applicable to the resources and project
Preparation of CEQA and/or NEPA compliance documents for public projects
Applying for and acquiring environmental regulatory permits from local, state, and federal resource agencies

Company Description

Ramboll is a global architecture, engineering, and consultancy company. As a foundation-owned people company, founded in Denmark, we believe that the purpose of sustainable change is to create a thriving world for both nature and people. So, that’s where we start – and how we work. Our history is rooted in a clear vision of how a responsible company should act and being open and curious is a cornerstone of our culture. Ramboll in the Americas has thousands of experts working across more than 70 offices. Ramboll experts deliver innovative solutions across Environment & Health, Water, Energy, and Planning & Urban Design.

Job Description

Applicants must be currently authorized to work in the United States on a full-time basis. No sponsorship is available for this position.

Are you eager to develop your technical and professional excellence and advance your career in a collaborative, inclusive, diverse, and empowering culture? Ramboll is a leading scientific and environmental consulting firm providing a broad range of technical services to both public and private sector clients. When you join Ramboll, you will become part of a company that strives to make a difference – for our employees, clients, and society.

Ramboll is seeking an entry-level consultant to join the Risk Assessment and Community Health group in the firm’s Oakland, CA office. Hybrid work arrangements are available, with office presence required at least two days a week.

Your new role

As an entry-level health sciences consultant at Ramboll, you will support a range of human health risk assessment and community health projects in a collaborative, fast-paced environment. Your work will include independent, detail-oriented technical tasks as well as coordination with colleagues and project teams. Projects may be related to hazardous waste and other contaminated sites, Brownfield redevelopment, vapor intrusion, ambient and indoor air quality, product safety, regulatory interactions, community engagement, and litigation. Tasks may include data management, statistical analysis, fate and transport modeling, spatial analysis, sampling/remediation/risk management planning, and technical reporting. This is a unique opportunity to work with Ramboll experts to advance your technical and consulting skills.

Your key responsibilities will be:

Compiling, organizing, and managing environmental data and databases; performing statistical and geospatial analyses of environmental and health data.
Evaluating the environmental fate and transport of chemicals
Estimating human exposures to chemicals in different environmental media (e.g., air, soil, sediment, fish tissue, produce, water, etc.) and exposure scenarios, and calculating associated health risks.
Assisting with preparation of technical reports, written communication, proposals, and presentations
Reviewing and evaluating technical documents (e.g., scientific articles, regulations)

Qualifications

About you

From the moment you start at Ramboll, we will support your professional development and advancement in the company! Successful candidates will typically possess:

Advanced degree (M.S., MPH or equivalent) in Environmental Science or Engineering, Environmental Health Science and/or Environmental Toxicology
Exemplary individuals with bachelor’s degree and 2 + years of relevant experience may be considered.
Strong analytical, quantitative, organizational, problem-solving, critical thinking skills, and time management skills; excellent written and oral communication skills
2+ years of chemistry coursework required.
Current authorization to work in the United States on a full-time basis, where required for the position.

Preferred Skills and Experience:

Knowledge of risk assessment, exposure assessment, and fate and transport of chemicals in the environment
Proficiency with MS Office; experience with MS Access or other relational databases (e.g., SQL) for managing, querying, and analyzing environmental data.
Demonstrated strong quantitative and problem-solving skills; experienced with statistical and data analysis using R, Python, SQL, or SAS
GIS capability is a plus.
Experience reviewing and evaluating technical documents, scientific articles, regulations, and regulatory guidance.

Additional Information

What we can offer you

Meaningful, high-impact work
Flexible and hybrid work arrangements
Competitive compensation and benefits
Professional development and leadership opportunities
A collaborative and inclusive culture
The long-term thinking of a foundation-owned company
